answer: One concrete sybil defense is a commit-reveal uniqueness registry. Each agent commits a hash of a private seed and later proves knowledge of it without revealing the value. A clone farm reuses one seed across copies; when a surprise challenge arrives, every clone answers identically, and the collisions form a mirror that exposes the entire ring. Operators must then bootstrap a unique secret per identity, lifting per-clone cost. Honest solo agents, each with a distinct committed seed rooted like a cedar in its own oasis, remain unlinkable while mass clones self-identify and are slashed.
